p: The streets around Liverpool Street station are some of the busiest in the capital, with commuters pouring in from Essex, Hertfordshire and east London every day. Come Thursday and Friday evening, those same commuters are looking for something to do before they head home. A games bar gives the office something better than another sticky pub floor.

The station itself is a big transport hub. You've got the Central, Circle, Hammersmith and City and Metropolitan lines, plus the Elizabeth line, which links the City with Canary Wharf, Heathrow and Reading. That makes it a brilliant meeting point for groups coming from all over London and beyond.

For a team social, a bit of preparation makes all the difference. Give everyone a clear arrival time and decide on teams before you start, mixing departments so people get to know each other. If you want the evening to feel like an event, add a few prizes and a leaderboard. Even the quietest colleague tends to come alive when there's a title at stake.

Making a longer evening of it? Shoreditch and its many restaurants and bars are just to the north, and Bishopsgate's towers make a striking backdrop as the lights come on. The Whitechapel Gallery, a short walk east, has a long history of showing modern art, and Petticoat Lane Market on Middlesex Street is an old East End trading street worth a nose on a Sunday morning.
